newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: EVANS SAYS ALP IS REMARKABLY UNIFIED
Deputy Opposition Leader, Gareth Evans, says unity has been one of the hallmarks of Labor's time in opposition.
Mr Evans was denying claims the Opposition is divided by sniping and treachery.
Labor leader, Kim Beazley, has called for more discipline and unity in the party, after a number of comments by some MPs to the media.
But Mr Evans says there is a strong degree of unanimity in the ALP, which he says is unusual for a party which has recently suffered a heavy defeat.
MEDIUM DENSITY HOUSING RISING IN POPULARITY
It appears Australians are getting more used to the idea of forgoing the house on the quarter acre block.

The latest quarterly monitor by the Australian Housing and Urban Research Institute reports that over the 18 months to last November, the acceptance of medium density housing rose from 61 to 66 percent.
In keeping with this, the proportion of households who find medium density housing unacceptable has fallen by five per cent to 29 percent.
The survey found that the in housing cost burdens is continuing to widen, with more than two-thirds of low income tenants paying more than 30 percent of their incomes on rent.
Purchasing a house with a mortgage depends largely on having two or more incomes.
NEW DROUGHT RELIEF SYSTEM TO BE WORKSHOPPED THIS WEEK
The Federal Government wants to establish a drought relief system that will enable farmers to salt money away during the good times, effectively saving for a non-rainy day.
Primary Industries Minister, John Anderson, will meet with state Agriculture Ministers this week, with discussions focusing on the establishment of a new national drought welfare system.
Mr Anderson says the new system would enable farmers to establish their own "financial haystacks" to draw on during financial downturns.
He says the existing programs are too complicated and not fair.
Drought relief payments, which were due to finish next week, have been extended to around 6,000 farmers while the government considers the new plan.
EVANS: PM AND TREASURER SEEM SPLIT ON TAX REFORM
The Federal Opposition says the Prime Minister and the Treasurer seem to be at odds over the value of tax reform as a job creation tool.
John Howard yesterday said tax reform is as important as labour reform and economic growth in boosting employment, but Treasurer, Peter Costello, says it is less important than other measures.
Labor's Treasury spokesman, Gareth Evans, says the Opposition agrees with Mr Costello.
Mr Evans says tax reform is not the main game, despite its billing by Mr Howard as one of the big three policy reforms required to get Australia back to work.
SA FED LIB BACKBENCHER THREATENS TO CROSS FLOOR ON TARIFFS
South Australian Federal Liberal M-P, Susan Jeanes, has again threatened to cross the floor of Parliament over the car tariffs issue.
Ms Jeanes holds Kingston, in Adelaide's south, by a margin of only 2.1 percent.
Many Mitsubishi car workers live in the electorate.
Her threat follows speculation that the Federal Government has reached an in-principle decision to cut tariffs from 15 per cent in 2000 to 10 per cent by 2005.

While that is not as drastic as the Productivity Commission's original recommendation for the car industry, Ms Jeanes says Julia Lester she will still cross the floor over the issue, if her constituents are not happy with the new position. - - - -
ALP TO OPPOSE CAR TARIFF COMPROMISE PLAN
The Federal Opposition says the Government will put half the car industry out of work if it compromises on proposals to cut tariffs, meeting the industry and the Productivity Commission halfway.
The commission wants tariffs to be cut to five per cent by 2005, but the industry and the Opposition say they should be lowered to 15 per cent, and then frozen.
Shadow Industry Minister Simon Crean says the Opposition will try to block any legislation to reduce tariffs to 10 per cent, a move the Government is reportedly considering.
Mr Crean says such legislation would not pass in the Senate.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
